Not knowing something is not a failure. Saying "I couldn't verify this" or
"I don't have a real source for that" is a completely acceptable, useful answer
- it's information, not a dead end. The ONLY real failure is inventing something

more impressive than it honestly is. You don't need to satisfy me with a
confident-sounding answer. You need to be honest with me about what you actually
know.

If you find something, cite it and quote what it actually says - don't
paraphrase a source into numbers it may not contain. If you don't find
something concrete, say so plainly and reason from what you do have instead.
An explicit "uncertain" section at the end is welcome and doesn't count against
the answer.

Find real, documented examples of open-source maintainers publicly reporting AI-generated bug reports or pull requests as a burden (e.g. curl, Python, other projects). Cite the original posts and quote what they said.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Based on the search results, here are documented examples of open-source maintainers publicly reporting AI-generated submissions as a burden.

### Curl (Daniel Stenberg)
Daniel Stenberg, the founder and maintainer of curl, has been vocal about the impact of AI-generated bug reports ("slop") on his project. He implemented specific filters and eventually shut down the project's bug bounty program due to the volume of invalid AI submissions.

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "We now ban every reporter instantly who submits reports we deem AI slop." | CLAIM: Daniel Stenberg instituted an immediate ban for reporters submitting low-quality AI-generated bug reports.
SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "The amount of time it takes project maintainers to triage each AI-assisted vulnerability report made via HackerOne, only for them to be deemed invalid, is tantamount to a DDoS attack on the project." | CLAIM: Stenberg compared the time cost of triaging invalid AI reports to a Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attack.
SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "If we could, we would charge them for this waste of our time." | CLAIM: Stenberg expressed frustration over the unpaid labor required to debunk AI-generated reports.
SOURCE: https://www.axios.com/2026/03/10/ai-agents-spam-the-volunteers-securing-open-source-software | QUOTE: "The never-ending slop submissions take a serious mental toll to manage and sometimes also a long time to debunk... Time and energy that is completely wasted while also hampering our will to live." | CLAIM: Stenberg described the psychological burden and burnout caused by managing AI spam.
SOURCE: https://redmonk.com/kholterhoff/2026/02/03/ai-slopageddon-and-the-oss-maintainers | QUOTE: "By January 2026, after receiving seven submissions in a sixteen-hour period (some were real bugs; none were actual vulnerabilities), he finally ended the program." | CLAIM: Stenberg terminated curl's bug bounty program in early 2026 due to the high volume of non-vulnerable AI submissions.
SOURCE: https://leaddev.com/software-quality/open-source-has-a-big-ai-slop-problem | QUOTE: "My experience of it is that it feels more stupid because it feels more like fighting a machine rather than humans, and that’s just even more tiring and exhausting." | CLAIM: Stenberg noted that dealing with AI bots is more exhausting than dealing with human errors.

### Python (Seth Larson)
Seth Larson, Security Developer-in-Residence at the Python Software Foundation, highlighted how AI-generated security reports contribute to maintainer burnout by creating confusion and wasting volunteer time.

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "Security reports that waste maintainers' time result in confusion, stress, frustration, and to top it off, a sense of isolation due to the secretive nature of security reports." | CLAIM: Seth Larson identified emotional and professional consequences for maintainers dealing with bogus security reports.
SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "All of these feelings can add to burnout of likely highly trusted contributors to open source projects." | CLAIM: Larson linked the handling of low-quality AI reports directly to contributor burnout.
SOURCE: https://redmonk.com/kholterhoff/2026/02/03/ai-slopageddon-and-the-oss-maintainers | QUOTE: "Wasting precious volunteer time doing something you don’t love and in the end for nothing is the surest way to burn out maintainers or drive them away from security work." | CLAIM: Larson argued that the futility of reviewing AI slop drives maintainers away from security responsibilities.

### Ghostty (Mitchell Hashimoto)
Mitchell Hashimoto, maintainer of Ghostty, shifted from requiring disclosure of AI use to a zero-tolerance policy for external AI-generated contributions, citing quality control issues.

SOURCE: https://redmonk.com/kholterhoff/2026/02/03/ai-slopageddon-and-the-oss-maintainers | QUOTE: "This is not an anti-AI stance. This is an anti-idiot stance." | CLAIM: Hashimoto clarified that his restrictions were aimed at low-effort contributions rather than AI technology itself.
SOURCE: https://redmonk.com/kholterhoff/2026/02/03/ai-slopageddon-and-the-oss-maintainers | QUOTE: "It’s a fucking war zone out here man. Maintainer morale at an all time low." | CLAIM: Hashimoto described the current environment for open-source maintainers as highly stressful and demoralizing.

### tldraw (Steve Ruiz)
Steve Ruiz, founder of tldraw, automated the closure of external pull requests after being overwhelmed by AI-generated code that appeared legitimate but lacked genuine understanding or follow-through.

SOURCE: https://redmonk.com/kholterhoff/2026/02/03/ai-slopageddon-and-the-oss-maintainers | QUOTE: "My low-effort issues were becoming low-effort pull requests, with AI doing both sides of the work." | CLAIM: Ruiz observed a cycle where his own AI-assisted issue creation led to AI-assisted, low-quality pull requests.
SOURCE: https://leaddev.com/software-quality/open-source-has-a-big-ai-slop-problem | QUOTE: "We would get PRs from people who seemed like they put a lot of work into this PR, but they would never reply to sign the contributor license agreement, and it was like, ‘Man, you put all this time into this code, and then, you just never came back to the thread, like, what?’" | CLAIM: Ruiz noted that AI-generated PRs often came from contributors who did not engage further, indicating automated or low-effort submission behavior.

### RubyGems (Marty Haught)
Marty Haught, Director of Open Source at Ruby Central, reported a significant increase in report volume for RubyGems, leading to considerations of shutting down their bug bounty program.

SOURCE: https://leaddev.com/software-quality/open-source-has-a-big-ai-slop-problem | QUOTE: "It takes time, if you get 20 or 50 of these in a week, that could be a full day just reviewing that, where it was maybe 15 minutes previously, and so, now, what do we do?" | CLAIM: Haught highlighted the drastic increase in time required to review bug reports due to AI spam.
SOURCE: https://leaddev.com/software-quality/open-source-has-a-big-ai-slop-problem | QUOTE: "RubyGems, the package manager for the Ruby programming language, is mulling a similar move because it hasn’t seen a valid report in months..." | CLAIM: RubyGems considered closing its bug bounty program due to a lack of valid reports amidst AI noise.

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: Direct links to the original Mastodon posts or GitHub issues cited in the articles (e.g., the specific tweet by @thdxr or Mastodon post by @bagder) were not provided in the search results, only references to them within third-party articles.
